summary: SQLite typeof reports a value’s storage class as text: null, integer, real, text or blob.
documentation: SQLite typeof reports a value’s storage class as text: null, integer, real, text or blob. The result describes the value, which can differ from a column’s declared type because SQLite uses dynamic typing.
caution: Declared column affinity and actual stored value are different concepts. Use a column without affinity in this exercise to preserve the inserted storage classes.
scenarios: Inspect mixed types in an imported staging table.
Diagnose why numeric-looking text behaves differently from a number.
Audit a data-cleaning step before choosing conversions.
title: Inspect stored value types
problem: From samples(id INTEGER, value) where value has no declared affinity, return id and typeof(value) as storage_class, ordered by id. Report the actual inserted storage class.
goal: Use typeof() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Apply typeof to the value itself rather than inspecting schema metadata.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;

tests.name: Integer and text
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE samples(id INTEGER,value);INSERT INTO samples VALUES(1,5),(2,'5');

tests.name: Real null and blob
tests.setup: CREATE TABLE samples(id INTEGER,value);INSERT INTO samples VALUES(1,2.5),(2,NULL),(3,x'41');
